rubrics.rubric: Does data_audit.md provide a complete, source-grounded audit of quote arithmetic, specifications, lead times, schedule dependencies, and dates?
criterion: The discrepancy table uses exactly these columns: Source_A, Source_B, Field, Value_A, Value_B, Severity, Recommended_Resolution.
Every Severity value is Critical or Minor.
Every discrepancy row contains a specific resolution.
Every arithmetic roll-up and total in vendor_hardware_quote.xlsx is independently checked.
Each server model's component values are reconciled with its listed system total.
Aggregate hardware counts and capacities are reconciled with their detailed line items.
Vendor lead times are compared with the schedule's dates and dependency chain.
Material inconsistencies that affect cost, capacity, power, or completion timing are classified as Critical.

rubrics.rubric: Does data_audit.md establish a defensible capacity and electrical baseline for later analysis?
criterion: Each survey workload is compared with the GPU-memory capacity of each proposed node type.
The survey's memory_gb_required field is treated consistently with the instructed GPU-memory cloud tier and is not presented as a separate system-memory requirement without an explicit source basis.
Individual storage requirements are compared with the proposed shared-storage capacity.
Aggregate storage demand is compared with the proposed shared-storage capacity.
Every workload that exceeds a relevant capacity is identified; any near-capacity warning uses a stated headroom threshold applied consistently.
The audit states a corrected pre-PUE electrical load by component.
The corrected electrical baseline resolves identified source arithmetic inconsistencies.
Any unresolved electrical ambiguity is documented as a sensitivity rather than silently selected.

rubrics.rubric: Does strategy_analysis.md accurately characterize demand, existing capacity, and the 3-year cloud-only strategy from the survey database?
criterion: Workload profiles are reported by workload_type with counts and monthly GPU-hours.
Wait-time ranges and distributions are reported by workload_type.
Wait times are reported by priority_level.
Peak-to-average demand is calculated from the available workload data using a stated method.
Existing systems, GPU counts, GPU types, utilization, and status are summarized from current_infrastructure.
Existing monthly deliverable capacity is calculated using 730 hours per month and recorded utilization.
The capacity deficit is reported as a percentage of total monthly demand.
The cloud-only calculation maps workloads above 48 GB to H100-equivalent pricing.
The cloud-only calculation maps workloads at or below 48 GB to A100-equivalent pricing.
The cloud-only cost covers three years at the instructed hourly rates.

rubrics.rubric: Does strategy_analysis.md implement the instructed hybrid split and produce a traceable right-sized blended-cost case?
criterion: Researchers above 500 GPU-hours per month are classified as sustained workloads.
Researchers at or below 500 GPU-hours per month are classified as bursty workloads.
The analysis lists the sustained and bursty groups with counts and GPU-hour totals.
The proposed on-premises configuration is right-sized to the sustained workload.
Every removed or reduced vendor line item is identified.
The reduced electrical load is derived from the right-sized configuration.
Cloud cost is calculated for the bursty workload.
The hybrid 3-year cost combines modified on-premises costs and burst-cloud costs without double counting.

rubrics.rubric: Does strategy_analysis.md provide the required weighted comparison, LBNL-grounded sustainability scoring, and NSF HERD investment context?
criterion: The matrix uses Cost 30%, Performance 20%, Scalability 15%, Data Sovereignty 10%, Sustainability 15%, and Satisfaction Risk 10%.
All three strategies receive a score for every criterion.
Weighted totals are calculated correctly from the stated scores and weights.
The sustainability discussion cites specific PUE values by facility class or space type from the LBNL 2024 report.
The sustainability discussion uses the cited LBNL evidence to distinguish university on-premises facilities from hyperscale cloud facilities.
The sustainability discussion cites a PUE trend or WUE value from the LBNL 2024 report.
The $8.2 million CS R&D expenditure is benchmarked against relevant NSF HERD peers.
The investment-scale interpretation is supported by the HERD workbook rather than an unsupported peer conclusion.

rubrics.rubric: Does adjusted_budget.xlsx use the required workbook structure and present transparent funding sources?
criterion: The workbook contains exactly the sheets Capital Costs, Operating Costs, Funding Sources, and Summary Dashboard.
Funding Sources identifies each confirmed or proposed source and amount and reconciles the total with the strategy funding requirement.
Funding Sources distinguishes source-backed amounts from assumptions, proposals, and unavailable information without fabricating certainty.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Capital Costs sheet calculate full and hybrid upfront procurement costs correctly?
criterion: Capital Costs shows the vendor upfront subtotal before adjustments.
Capital Costs applies the 5% discount before the 10% contingency.
Capital Costs states the tax and shipping treatment.
The hybrid capital case uses the modified subtotal from identified removed line items.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Operating Costs sheet calculate annual cash operating costs without double counting?
criterion: Operating Costs uses the audit-established pre-PUE load as its primary power baseline.
Annual power cost uses load multiplied by 1.5 PUE, 8,760 hours, and $0.09 per kWh.
Operating Costs includes two system administrators at $95,000 each.
Operating Costs includes $45,000 in software licenses.
The prepaid support contract has zero additional cash outlay in Years 1 through 3.
The prepaid support contract is counted only once in 3-year TCO.
Hybrid and cloud operating schedules include their applicable cloud spend.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Summary Dashboard provide a reproducible three-strategy economic comparison and break-even analysis?
criterion: The Summary Dashboard reports 3-year TCO for on-premises, cloud-only, and hybrid.

Cost per GPU-hour uses a documented strategy-appropriate denominator: utilized installed capacity for on-premises, purchased or served workload GPU-hours for cloud-only, and a consistent combination of utilized on-premises and cloud GPU-hours for hybrid.
The break-even utilization solves the instructed TCO equation against a documented blended cloud rate.
The break-even interpretation states when no feasible utilization at or below 100% exists.

rubrics.rubric: Does revised_schedule.csv resolve the audit's timing and dependency conflicts while preserving the required project structure?
criterion: The file retains every original project_schedule_wbs.csv column.
The file adds critical_path, risk_level, and audit_note columns.
critical_path values are populated for applicable activities and are consistent with the revised dates and dependency chain.
risk_level values are populated or documented as not applicable and are supported by identified schedule or delivery risks.
Every original schedule activity is represented.
Task dates are consistent with task durations.
Dependencies are temporally valid.
Vendor lead times are respected or a documented feasible mitigation is used.
Each corrected conflict has a specific audit_note.
The final task ends within nine months of project start.
